sections.normalization: The stage that standardizes network inputs and targets so that every channel trains on a comparable numeric range. It fits one location and scale per channel on the train split, persists them with the run, and inverts the target transform when predictions are scored. The configs here choose the fitting method for the inputs and for the targets and describe the persisted per-channel statistics.
sections.dataset: The stage that turns a dataset directory into trainable examples. It crops every split region from the input and target arrays, tiles the regions into overlapping patches with a per-pixel weight map, applies augmentation to the train split and builds the train, validation and test dataloaders. The configs here control patch tiling, augmentation, normalization and the loaders.
sections.architectures: The stage that defines the backbone architectures. Each config specifies one model variant's layer geometry and per-group optimizer settings. The configs here cover convolutional and transformer backbones that predict every target channel at every pixel.
sections.training: The stage that optimizes the backbone. It binds architecture, loss, optimization, scheduling, and runtime sub-configs into one resolved run and manages queuing and sweeps. The configs here control loss term weighting, optimizer, scheduler, warmup, early-stopping and gradient-clipping policy, filesystem layout, VRAM reservation and resource monitoring, and the trainer and entry configs.
sections.resources: Host and device sampling settings shared by every training family: whether the resource monitor runs, how often it samples CPU, RAM, shared memory and GPU memory, whether samples go to TensorBoard, and the utilisation levels that raise a warning in the run log. They live outside the training package so that a long-running processing entry can carry them without importing torch.
sections.inference: The stage that runs trained checkpoints over data splits to produce predictions, evaluations, and reports. It drives sliding-window prediction for backbone runs, scheduling one worker per run across a GPU pool. The configs here control the per-run inference driver, its output subdirectory and filename layout, and the batch entry point that queues inference across all discovered runs.
sections.benchmark: The stage that compares multiple model architectures on the same data. It trains each backbone at its own configured size, runs inference, and assembles a cross-model comparison report. The configs here control batched inference and its diagnostic artifacts, the comparison report assembly, and the top-level sweep orchestration.
sections.cross_validation: The stage that estimates generalization by partitioning the dataset rows into k folds and training and evaluating on each. It orchestrates per-fold training, inference, and comparison for the backbone. The configs here control the row-range fold partitioning and the top-level k-fold orchestration.
sections.tuning: The stage that searches hyperparameter spaces with Optuna to improve a chosen backbone. It wires the search budget, pruning, and resources to a nested training configuration and swaps in per-trial hyperparameter samples. The configs here control the Optuna search controls and artifact emission, and the entry point binding resources and data to the search.
sections.comparison: The stage that rebuilds side-by-side comparisons across completed runs and trials without re-running training or inference. It aggregates existing inference outputs into a single report grouped by the varied factor. The configs here control the comparison of trial runs, the aggregation of seed runs, and the standalone rebuild of an existing benchmark comparison report.
sections.diagnostics: The stage that inspects completed training runs independently of any data run. The weight-xray diagnostic classifies each checkpoint tensor against numeric thresholds and emits a per-run report and plots; the tensorboard export renders every logged scalar series as a publication-quality figure inside the run directory, pairing train and validation series of the same metric in one shared figure. The configs here control the pathology classification thresholds, the single-run diagnostics and their report and plot outputs, and the batch webui entries that select runs and build a per-run configuration.
sections.generation: The stage that writes the bundled example dataset, so the template runs end to end without external data. It draws a few smooth random input fields with noise, computes target fields from them with a known nonlinear and spatially local function, splits the grid into train, validation and test row bands, and writes dataset.json, inputs.npy and targets.npy. The configs here control the grid size, the number of input channels, the smoothness and neighbourhood of the fields, the noise levels and the split fractions.

fields.resume_from: Path at or inside an existing cross-validation run to finish (the run directory, its pipeline, folds or one fold run inside it). The run recorded configuration under pipeline/resolved_config.json is loaded as the base, the overrides typed on this launch are applied on top, the run tag and log base follow the path, and resume is switched on; every fold x seed unit is matched to its directory through the unit manifest it wrote, so only the missing or unfinished units and inference splits run. Empty starts a fresh run
fields.loss: LossConfig every fold trains under, defaulting to the training entry's loss

tuning/general::TuningConfig.summary: Optuna hyperparameter search controls: trial budget, seeding, pruning, and artifact emission

fields.n_trials: target number of completed trials per model's Optuna study, resumable across runs (existing completed/pruned trials count toward it)
fields.n_epochs: training epochs evaluated per trial before scoring it, applied to both the training loop and its LR scheduler
fields.base_seed: base RNG seed: offset by the worker index seeds the Optuna TPE sampler, offset by trial number seeds each trial's weight init and augmentation
fields.early_stop_patience: epochs without validation improvement before a trial's training is halted early
fields.pruner_n_startup_trials: startup-trial count shared by optuna.pruners.MedianPruner (trials exempt from pruning) and the TPESampler (trials of random search before it switches to TPE)
fields.pruner_n_warmup_steps: epochs within a trial before MedianPruner is allowed to prune that trial
fields.search_lr: Whether the study samples the model configuration's learning rates, weight decays and dropout (its tunable_lr_params). Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.search_arch: Whether the study samples the model configuration's architecture fields (its tunable_arch_params: feature widths, bottleneck factor, activation, normalization, upsampling and the like). Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.search_batch: Whether the study samples the training batch size from batch_sizes. The trial puts the drawn size on the loader and rescales the optimizer by batch over lr_reference_batch_size as every training entry does, so a tuned rate stays quoted at the reference batch and a downstream run with the same batch reproduces it. The best size is recorded on a training.batch_size decision axis of a sequence block. Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.batch_sizes: Batch sizes the study may pick when search_batch is on; every size must fit the GPU with the largest architecture the study may draw. Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.plateau_patience: Finished trials (completed or pruned) without the best value improving before the study stops; 0 runs the trial target out. The finished trials are walked in trial order, a completed trial beating the best by at least plateau_min_delta resets the count, and every worker reads the same verdict off the shared study. Changeable on resume
fields.plateau_min_delta: Smallest improvement of the best value, relative to its value at the last counted improvement, that resets the plateau count; 0 counts any improvement, which lets seed noise keep a converged study alive. Changeable on resume
fields.time_budget_h: Hours after which a worker starts no further trial; the trial in flight still finishes, so a launch with a hard time limit must allow the budget plus one trial. 0 sets no budget. Changeable on resume
fields.emit_trial_docs: whether to write per-trial training-documentation artifacts to the run directory
fields.emit_study_plots: whether to render Optuna study-level visualization plots after each model's sweep completes
fields.keep_trial_checkpoints: Whether the checkpoint files (best_model.pt, last.pt, final_model.pt, epoch snapshots) of a finished trial stay in its run directory. Off by default: nothing loads them again, the trial's parameters live in the study, and a study of hundreds of trials would otherwise hold hundreds of gigabytes of weights that a sequence workspace pull copies back

tuning/general::TuningEntryConfig.summary: Entry point wiring an Optuna tuning sweep: model type, resources, data, and nested search/training configs

fields.stage: Part of the run to execute. 'prepare' only creates the studies, so trial workers launched separately have something to attach to; 'compare' only writes the best configuration and the study plots of studies the workers filled; 'full' runs the trials between the two, which is what a local launch does
fields.paths: RunPathsConfig sub-config holding the dataset directory and the log and output base directory shared by every trial
fields.tuning: TuningConfig sub-config controlling the Optuna search (trial count, epochs, pruning, seeding)
fields.gpus: list of GPU device indices across which each model's trials are distributed and run in parallel
fields.n_workers: Trial workers each study is fanned out over. Zero means one worker per device in the GPU pool, which is what a local launch can keep busy at once; a launch whose pool is sized elsewhere sets the count explicitly
fields.gpus_file: Path of the live GPU pool control file for this queue; the scheduler seeds it from the gpus selection and re-reads it on every poll, so writing {"gpus": [...]} into it resizes the run while it is in flight (added devices pick up queued jobs, removed devices retire once the job in flight ends). Empty places gpu_pool.json inside the run directory
fields.skip_models: model names excluded from the sweep's registry-driven model loop
fields.run_tag: optional label naming this sweep's run directory and Optuna study/database, defaults to a timestamp
fields.training: TrainingQueueConfig sub-config supplying the base training-loop/queue settings (epochs, batch size, LR schedule, clipping, splits) shared across all trials
fields.normalization: NormalizationConfig sub-config controlling per-channel input/output normalization strategy shared by all backbone trials
fields.augmentation: AugmentationConfig sub-config setting flip/rot90/noise probabilities applied to training patches across all backbone trials
fields.resume_from: Path at or inside an existing tuning run to continue (the run directory or any path inside it). The run recorded configuration beside its Optuna database is loaded as the base, the overrides typed on this launch are applied on top, the run tag and log base follow the path, and every study is topped up to the trial target; the study-defining fields stay guarded exactly as with --resume. Empty starts a fresh run
fields.loss: LossConfig every tuning trial trains under, defaulting to the training entry's loss

comparison::TrialComparisonConfig.summary: Entry config for comparing inference outputs across multiple backbone training runs; a trial with nested seed runs is compared as one seed-aggregated entry (metric means with sample-std annotations)

fields.runs_dir: Root directory holding the backbone training run subdirectories to compare
fields.run_tags: Run subfolder names to compare; a trial directory name expands to its nested seed<N> runs which aggregate into one seed-mean entry, and the collector only processes the listed tags without auto-scanning runs_dir, so an empty list yields zero trials
fields.inference_split: Dataset split whose completed inference directory supplies each trial's metrics; a run carrying inference for several splits contributes only the newest stamp whose completion marker records this split
fields.compare_images: Whether to render static side-by-side image comparisons across the collected runs
fields.embed_images: Base64-embed figures inline in the generated markdown report instead of linking external files
fields.output_dir: Destination for the comparison report; None writes to a _comparison subfolder under runs_dir

comparison::SeedComparisonConfig.summary: Entry config that aggregates the existing inference results of the seed runs nested inside each selected group directory into a mean ± std seed-comparison report per group, without re-running inference

fields.runs_dir: Root directory the group directories are resolved against; with group_tags empty it is itself treated as the single seed group to aggregate
fields.group_tags: Group directory names relative to runs_dir, each the shared training run directory holding one sweep's seed<N> runs; every selected group is compared in isolation and its report generated in sequence, an unmatched name raises FileNotFoundError, and empty treats runs_dir itself as one group
fields.split: Data split every aggregated inference stamp must record in its completion marker (train, val or test); a seed whose newest completed stamp was scored on another split is refused, so one aggregate never mixes splits
fields.inference_subdir: Fixed inference stamp to read from every seed run (run_dir/inference/<subdir>); it must carry a completion marker for the configured split and a metrics file, and empty picks each run's newest completed stamp of that split, skipping stamps without a completion marker with a warning
fields.output_subdir: Name of the aggregate output directory written under each group's inference/ subdirectory; empty falls back to inference_subdir when set, else a fresh timestamp shared by all groups
fields.metrics_filename: Filename of the per-run metrics JSON read from each seed's inference directory and of the aggregate mean/std JSON written next to the report
fields.report_filename: Filename of the generated seed-comparison markdown report, also used to link each seed's own report
fields.compute_disagreement: Also compute the per-pixel across-seed standard deviation of every predicted target channel from the saved inference maps, with a risk-coverage curve and a label-suspect map, written beside the report; needs inference run with save_maps
fields.compute_ensemble: Also average every seed's saved prediction maps into one deep-ensemble prediction and score it against the targets with the same per-channel metrics, reported next to the per-seed mean; needs inference run with save_maps
fields.maps_subdir: Name of the maps subdirectory inside each seed's inference directory that holds predictions.npy and targets.npy, read by the ensemble and the disagreement maps

comparison::ComparisonPathsConfig.summary: Locates the benchmark run directory for a standalone comparison rebuild

fields.log_base_dir: Root directory holding the benchmark run directories, defaults to RunPathsConfig.log_base_dir

comparison::ComparisonEntryConfig.summary: Entry config that rebuilds the benchmark comparison report for an existing run without re-running training or inference

fields.run_tag: Benchmark run tag to compare; None picks the most recent run with a training subdirectory under log_base_dir
fields.embed_images: Base64-embed figures inline in the generated markdown report instead of linking external files
fields.inference_split: Dataset split whose completed inference stamps supply each model's metrics in the rebuilt comparison; defaults to test, the split a full benchmark scores last
fields.paths: ComparisonPathsConfig sub-config giving the benchmark log_base_dir the run_tag is resolved against

diagnostics::WeightXrayThresholds.summary: Numeric thresholds classifying weight-tensor pathologies during the weight-xray checkpoint diagnostic

fields.dead_abs_threshold: absolute magnitude below which any analyzed tensor's element counts as dead, feeds the per-tensor frac_dead statistic
fields.dead_fraction_warn: frac_dead level at or above which a tensor is flagged high_sparsity (warning), 0.50 default
fields.dead_fraction_critical: frac_dead level at or above which a tensor is flagged dead_tensor (critical), 0.95 default
fields.dead_unit_norm_frac: fraction of a weight matrix's max row/column norm at or below which that output or input unit counts as dead
fields.dead_unit_fraction_warn: fraction of dead output units (dead_output_frac) at or above which dead_neurons is a warning instead of info
fields.uniform_cv_threshold: coefficient-of-variation (std/mean_abs) at or below which weight or norm_scale tensors of 8+ elements flag as near-uniform
fields.constant_std_threshold: tensor standard deviation at or below which it is flagged critical as constant
fields.rank_ratio_warn: effective-to-full rank ratio at or below which a weight matrix flags rank_deficient (warning), 0.50 default
fields.rank_ratio_critical: effective-to-full rank ratio at or below which a weight matrix flags rank_collapse (critical), 0.10 default
fields.explode_abs_threshold: max absolute value in any analyzed tensor at or above which it flags large_magnitude (warning)
fields.spectral_norm_warn: top singular value of a weight matrix at or above which it flags large_spectral_norm (warning)
fields.bias_abs_threshold: max absolute bias value at or above which a bias tensor flags large_bias (warning)
fields.norm_scale_dead_value: absolute value below which a normalization-layer scale (gamma) element counts as collapsed
fields.norm_scale_dead_frac: fraction of norm-scale elements below norm_scale_dead_value at or above which scale_collapse warns
fields.running_var_dead_value: BatchNorm running_var value below which a channel counts as dead
fields.running_var_dead_frac: fraction of running_var elements below running_var_dead_value at or above which dead_channel_var warns
fields.init_ratio_low: lower bound on std*sqrt(fan_in) below which a weight raises an info scale_low observation
fields.init_ratio_high: upper bound on std*sqrt(fan_in) above which a weight raises an info scale_high observation
fields.duplicate_cosine: absolute cosine similarity between two normalized output-unit rows at or above which they count as a duplicate pair
fields.duplicate_fraction_warn: ratio of duplicate-pair count to output-unit count at or above which duplicate_units is a warning instead of info

diagnostics::WeightXrayConfig.summary: Runtime settings for a single weight-xray checkpoint diagnostic run and its report/plot outputs

fields.checkpoint_path: checkpoint file or run directory to analyze, defaults to logs; when a directory, checkpoint_filename is appended
fields.output_dir: base directory where the weight-xray markdown/json report and plots subdirectory are written, defaults to results/weight_xray
fields.checkpoint_filename: checkpoint filename appended to checkpoint_path when it points at a directory, defaults to best_model.pt
fields.state_dict_keys: candidate top-level dict keys tried in order to locate the parameter tensor mapping inside a loaded checkpoint, defaults to ["params"]
fields.thresholds: WeightXrayThresholds sub-config bundling the numeric pathology-classification thresholds used during analysis
fields.svd_max_dim: min(out_units, fan_in) above which SVD-based rank and spectral-norm stats are skipped to bound compute cost
fields.duplicate_max_units: max output-unit count above which duplicate-unit detection is skipped to bound the pairwise gram-matrix cost
fields.histogram_sample_max: max samples pooled into the global weight histogram; larger pools are evenly subsampled via linspace indexing
fields.max_layer_histograms: max number of per-layer histograms rendered, taken from the flagged (warning/critical) weight tensors
fields.make_plots: whether to render all diagnostic plots (per-tensor L2/std/sparsity/rank-ratio series plus weight histograms) via WeightXrayPlots
fields.embed_images: whether to base64-embed the diagnostic plot images inline in the markdown report instead of linking external files

diagnostics::WeightXrayEntryConfig.summary: Batch webui entry selecting backbone runs and building a per-run WeightXrayConfig via to_config

fields.runs_dir: parent directory recursively scanned (rglob) by RunSelector for run subdirectories containing checkpoint_filename to x-ray
fields.run_filter: exact run names or run-dir relative paths selecting which runs under runs_dir to x-ray; empty triggers interactive selection on a tty, else all runs
fields.checkpoint_filename: checkpoint filename expected inside each run directory, defaults to best_model.pt
fields.output_subdir: subdirectory name inside each run directory where that run's weight-xray report and plots are written
fields.make_plots: whether to render diagnostic plots, forwarded to each run's WeightXrayConfig.make_plots
fields.embed_images: whether to inline images into the markdown report, forwarded to each run's WeightXrayConfig.embed_images
fields.thresholds: WeightXrayThresholds sub-config holding every detection threshold, forwarded unchanged into each run's WeightXrayConfig
fields.svd_max_dim: max matrix dimension for computing SVD-based rank/spectral stats, forwarded to each run's WeightXrayConfig
fields.duplicate_max_units: max output-unit count scanned for duplicates, forwarded to each run's WeightXrayConfig
fields.max_layer_histograms: max number of per-layer histograms rendered per run, forwarded to each run's WeightXrayConfig

diagnostics::TensorboardExportConfig.summary: Per-run tensorboard plot export: reads the run's tensorboard event log and renders every scalar series as a publication-quality figure inside the run directory, mirroring the tag hierarchy as folders; train and validation series of the same metric share one figure

fields.run_directory: training run directory holding the tensorboard event log; the exported plots are written inside it
fields.tensorboard_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside the run directory that holds the tensorboard event files, defaults to tensorboard
fields.output_subdir: subdirectory name inside the run directory where the exported figures are written, defaults to tensorboard_plots

diagnostics::TensorboardExportEntryConfi.summary: Batch webui entry selecting training runs with tensorboard event logs and building a per-run TensorboardExportConfig via to_config; when sibling seed runs of one trial are selected, the trial directory additionally receives seed-overlay figures with every seed's curve per metric

fields.runs_dir: parent directory recursively scanned (rglob) by TensorboardRunSelector for run subdirectories whose tensorboard_dirname holds event files
fields.run_filter: exact run names or run-dir relative paths selecting which runs under runs_dir to export; a trial directory name expands to every seed run nested beneath it, empty triggers interactive selection on a tty, else all runs
fields.tensorboard_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside each run directory that holds the tensorboard event files, forwarded to each run's TensorboardExportConfig
fields.output_subdir: subdirectory name inside each run directory where that run's exported figures are written, forwarded to each run's TensorboardExportConfig

diagnostics::ReportCollectionConfig.summary: Per-run report collection: locates the run's inference report(s), rewrites every image link to an absolute path into the original figures (or embeds them as base64 data for a self-contained file), and writes the result into the collector directory renamed after the run

fields.run_directory: training run directory whose inference outputs hold the report(s) to collect
fields.collector_dir: directory that receives the collected report, named <run>.md (latest_only) or <run>_<inference tag>.md
fields.inference_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside the run directory that holds the timestamped inference outputs, defaults to inference
fields.report_filename: report filename inside each inference output directory, defaults to report.md
fields.latest_only: collect only the report of the latest inference output (by directory name); when false every inference report is collected with the inference tag appended to the name

diagnostics::ReportCollectionEntryConfig.summary: Batch webui entry selecting training runs with inference reports and building a per-run ReportCollectionConfig via to_config; nested seed runs are labelled <trial>_seed<N>, and a missing referenced image or two selected runs sharing a label abort the collection loudly

fields.runs_dir: parent directory recursively scanned (rglob) by ReportRunSelector for run subdirectories whose inference_dirname holds a report
fields.run_filter: exact run names or run-dir relative paths selecting which runs under runs_dir to collect; a trial directory name expands to every seed run nested beneath it, empty triggers interactive selection on a tty, else all runs
fields.collector_dir: single directory that receives every collected report, created if missing; re-collection overwrites previous copies
fields.inference_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside each run directory that holds the timestamped inference outputs, forwarded to each run's ReportCollectionConfig
fields.report_filename: report filename inside each inference output directory, forwarded to each run's ReportCollectionConfig
fields.latest_only: collect only each run's latest inference report; when false every inference report is collected with the inference tag appended to the name
fields.embed_images: embed referenced images as base64 data URIs so each collected report is fully self-contained instead of linking back to the original run figures

diagnostics::ExperimentReportMailConfig.summary: Gathering settings of one experiment's mail bundle: the staging directory, the comparison layout, the inference report layout, the regeneration switch and the image embedding mode

fields.staging_dir: directory that receives this experiment's gathered files; re-gathering overwrites previous copies
fields.comparison_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside the experiment holding the timestamped trial-comparison outputs, defaults to _comparison
fields.comparison_reports: report filenames gathered from the newest comparison stamp; a missing one aborts the gathering loudly
fields.inference_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside a trial that holds the timestamped inference outputs, defaults to inference
fields.report_filename: report filename inside each inference output directory, defaults to report.md
fields.regenerate_reports: whether the seed aggregates, the trial comparison and a cross-validation run's cross-fold report are rewritten even when present
fields.embed_images: embed referenced images as base64 data URIs so each gathered report is fully self-contained instead of linking back to the original figures by absolute path

diagnostics::ArtifactMailConfig.summary: Per-source artifact gathering for a dataset or a training run: resolves the path lists against the source directory, drops whatever the exclusion rules leave out, packs the rest into deflate archives that each stay under the attachment cap, and keeps the source tree inside them so unpacking every archive into one folder rebuilds it

fields.source_dir: dataset folder or training run folder whose artifacts are packed
fields.staging_dir: directory that receives this source's archives; re-gathering deletes the archives of the previous run first
fields.label: identity of the source in the subject line and the root folder every archived file sits under, also the stem of the archive filenames with the slash replaced by a double underscore
fields.required_paths: paths relative to the source directory that must exist, each a file or a directory whose whole subtree is taken; a missing one aborts the gathering loudly
fields.optional_paths: paths relative to the source directory attached when present, each a file or a directory whose whole subtree is taken; a missing one only warns
fields.excluded_paths: globs of content never packed, matched against a file's path relative to the source directory, against each of its parent directories and against the bare name of each of them, so 'maps' drops a directory of that name wherever it sits while 'inference/*/maps' drops only the ones inside an inference stamp
fields.excluded_suffixes: file extensions never packed, matched case-insensitively against the file name, .pt for the checkpoints and .npy for the arrays among them
fields.max_file_mb: upper bound of one packed file in megabytes, above which the file is left out and named in the left-out table; zero turns the size rule off and packs every file the other two rules keep
fields.max_attachment_mb: upper bound of one archive in megabytes, measured on the uncompressed sources; keep it under the mail server limit with room for the roughly one third that base64 encoding adds on the wire

diagnostics::ReportMailEntryConfig.summary: Entry config of the report mailer: picks one of three targets (experiments, runs, datasets), names the path each target scans and how each source is gathered, and carries the shared SMTP settings, the staging directory and the attachment size cap

fields.target: which source the run mails: experiments (sweeps of trial runs, cross-validation runs and benchmark runs found at or below experiments_dir), runs (the content of the training runs found at or below runs_dir) or datasets (generated datasets); only that target's root, filter and gathered paths are read
fields.experiments_dir: path searched for experiments at or below it: a sweep directory of trial runs, a cross-validation run (or its folds directory), a benchmark run (or its training directory), a sequence workspace holding several of them, or a whole runs tree; experiments are recognised by the trial runs they hold, never by their names, and the scan stops at each one so run trees are never entered
fields.experiment_filter: experiment paths relative to experiments_dir, or experiment names, restricting the mailing; empty mails every experiment found
fields.comparison_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside each sweep holding the timestamped trial-comparison outputs, where a missing comparison is written before mailing
fields.comparison_reports: report filenames gathered from the newest trial-comparison stamp of a sweep or cross-validation run (a benchmark run always contributes benchmark_overview.md and metrics_comparison.md from its own comparison); a missing one aborts
fields.inference_dirname: name of the subdirectory inside a trial that holds the timestamped inference outputs, forwarded to each experiment's ExperimentReportMailConfig
fields.report_filename: report filename inside each inference output directory, forwarded to each experiment's ExperimentReportMailConfig
fields.regenerate_reports: whether every selected experiment gets its seed-aggregate reports, its trial comparison and, for a cross-validation run, its cross-fold report rewritten even when they exist; off writes only the ones that are missing
fields.embed_images: embed referenced images as base64 data URIs so each gathered report is fully self-contained instead of linking back to the original figures by absolute path
fields.runs_dir: path searched for training runs at or below it, a whole runs tree, one family directory, a sweep or a single run; a run is recognised by the meta directory it holds and is never descended into, so the seed runs of a trial are offered as the separate runs they are
fields.run_filter: run paths relative to runs_dir, or run names, restricting the mailing; empty triggers interactive selection on a tty, else every run found
fields.run_excluded_paths: globs of a run's content never mailed, matched against a file's path relative to the run, against each of its parent directories and against the bare name of each of them; the default drops the checkpoints directory and every maps directory, wherever they sit
fields.run_excluded_suffixes: file extensions of a run's content never mailed; the default drops the checkpoints (.pt, .pth, .ckpt) and the arrays (.npy, .npz, .h5, .pkl), which is everything that runs to hundreds of megabytes
fields.run_max_file_mb: upper bound of one mailed file of a run in megabytes, above which it is left out and named in the left-out table; the default of 5 keeps every figure and leaves the walk animations behind, and zero mails every file the two exclusion lists keep
fields.datasets_dir: root directory holding one folder per generated dataset; only direct children carrying a data/dataset.json layout are offered
fields.dataset_filter: exact dataset folder names selecting which datasets to mail; empty triggers interactive selection on a tty, else all datasets
fields.dataset_required_paths: dataset generation outputs that must exist in a dataset, each a file or a directory whose whole subtree is attached; a missing one aborts that dataset loudly
fields.dataset_optional_paths: dataset generation outputs attached when present; a missing one only warns. The arrays under data/ are deliberately absent from the default: they run to hundreds of megabytes and would need dozens of messages
fields.staging_dir: directory that receives the gathered files, one subfolder per source; re-gathering overwrites the previous copies and deletes the archives of the previous run
fields.max_attachment_mb: upper bound of one archive in megabytes, measured on the uncompressed sources; a run or dataset whose artifacts exceed it is split across as many messages as it needs, and a single file above it aborts loudly. Keep it under the mail server limit with room for the roughly one third that base64 encoding adds on the wire
fields.recipient: address every message is sent to, taken from the machine profile when one sets it
fields.sender: address the messages are sent from, also used as the SMTP login user, taken from the machine profile when one sets it
fields.smtp_host: SMTP server the messages are submitted to over SSL, defaults to smtp.gmail.com
fields.smtp_port: SSL port of the SMTP server, defaults to 465
fields.smtp_timeout_s: seconds a blocking SMTP connect, login or upload may stall before the submission fails with a timeout instead of hanging; each message logs its size before the submission and its duration after it, defaults to 300
fields.password_env: name of the environment variable holding the SMTP password (for Gmail, an app password); the password itself is never stored in the config, and an unset variable aborts a real send
fields.subject_prefix: prefix of every message subject, followed by a colon and the source label, and by the part number when a bundle is split across several messages
fields.dry_run: stage and log every message without opening an SMTP connection; needs no password and is the way to preview what would be sent

diagnostics::ReceptiveFieldConfig.summary: Entry config that measures the effective receptive field of one or more trained backbone runs on real data: probe pixels across the split region, gradient of the centre output magnitude w.r.t. the input window, ERF sigma per axis and a gradient-mass ladder, written into each run directory

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for run directories holding the configured checkpoint file; each selected run is measured in sequence

fields.device: Torch device the model runs on; cpu is enough for the handful of probe windows and batches
fields.checkpoint_name: Checkpoint filename loaded from each run directory and used as the run-discovery marker
fields.output_subdir: Name of the output directory created inside each run directory for the JSON, figures and markdown report
fields.window: Side length in pixels of the square probe window the gradients are computed over; it has to fit inside the split region
fields.n_row_probes: Number of probe pixels along row, spread evenly across the split region with a window/2 margin
fields.n_col_probes: Number of probe pixels along cols, spread evenly across the split region with a window/2 margin
fields.occlude: Also run the occlusion pass: zero one normalized input channel at a time over a few batches and measure the mean squared shift of the normalized prediction against the unoccluded prediction
fields.batch_size: Batch size of the occlusion forward passes
fields.max_batches: Number of loader batches the occlusion deltas are averaged over; cost scales with channels x batches
fields.figure_style: PlotBase figure style the bar charts are rendered with (report or paper)

diagnostics::LayerProbeConfig.summary: Entry config that trains ridge linear probes on the intermediate features of one or more trained backbone runs, reporting held-out R² by depth for every target channel, written into each run directory

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for run directories holding the configured checkpoint file; each selected run is probed in sequence
fields.run_filter: Run directory names (or names of parent directories whose nested runs are expanded) to probe; empty selects interactively on a TTY and every discovered run otherwise
fields.split: Dataset split the probe batches and sampled pixels are drawn from
fields.device: Torch device the model runs on during feature capture
fields.checkpoint_name: Checkpoint filename loaded from each run directory and used as the run-discovery marker
fields.output_subdir: Name of the output directory created inside each run directory for the JSON, depth figures and markdown report
fields.batch_size: Batch size of the capture forward passes
fields.max_batches: Number of loader batches whose activations feed the probes; more batches mean more probe samples at linear cost
fields.max_layers: Maximum number of leaf layers probed, spread evenly across the network depth
fields.samples_per_batch: Number of weighted pixels sampled per batch as probe examples; padding pixels are never sampled; features are read at each pixel's location scaled into every layer's spatial grid
fields.ridge_lambda: Ridge regularization strength of the linear probes
fields.seed: Seed of the sampled probe pixels and of the held-out probe split; vary it to check how sensitive the reported R² is to the sample
fields.figure_style: PlotBase figure style the decodability curves are rendered with (report or paper)
fields.n_folds: Number of cross-validation folds the ridge probe averages its held-out R² over

diagnostics::LossLandscapeConfig.summary: Entry config that maps the weighted-MSE landscape around the trained weights of one or more backbone runs along two filter-normalized random directions, with 1D cuts, a 2D contour and sharpness scalars per run

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for run directories holding the configured checkpoint file; each selected run is mapped in sequence
fields.run_filter: Run directory names (or names of parent directories whose nested runs are expanded) to map; empty selects interactively on a TTY and every discovered run otherwise
fields.split: Dataset split the fixed evaluation batches are drawn from
fields.device: Torch device the perturbed model evaluations run on
fields.checkpoint_name: Checkpoint filename loaded from each run directory and used as the run-discovery marker
fields.output_subdir: Name of the output directory created inside each run directory for the JSON, figures and markdown report
fields.batch_size: Batch size of the fixed evaluation batches
fields.max_batches: Number of batches the weighted MSE is averaged over at every grid point; total cost scales with n_points squared times batches
fields.span: Half-width of the sampled step range along each filter-normalized direction
fields.n_points_1d: Number of grid points of each 1D cut
fields.n_points_2d: Number of grid points per axis of the 2D contour; the grid costs n_points_2d squared evaluations
fields.direction_seed: Seed of the two random directions (seed and seed+1); fixed seeds make landscapes comparable across runs
fields.figure_style: PlotBase figure style the cuts and contour are rendered with (report or paper)
fields.n_directions: Number of filter-normalized random directions the 1-D cuts and sharpness statistics average over; the first two also span the 2-D grid

diagnostics::RobustnessConfig.summary: Entry config that stresses one or more trained backbone runs with controlled input degradation: weighted MSE versus noise severity, gain error, number of dropped input channels and row shift, written into each run directory

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for run directories holding the configured checkpoint file; each selected run is stressed in sequence
fields.run_filter: Run directory names (or names of parent directories whose nested runs are expanded) to stress; empty selects interactively on a TTY and every discovered run otherwise
fields.split: Dataset split the fixed evaluation batches are drawn from
fields.device: Torch device the perturbed evaluations run on
fields.checkpoint_name: Checkpoint filename loaded from each run directory and used as the run-discovery marker
fields.output_subdir: Name of the output directory created inside each run directory for the JSON, curves and markdown report
fields.batch_size: Batch size of the fixed evaluation batches
fields.max_batches: Number of batches the weighted MSE is averaged over at every severity level
fields.noise_sigmas: Normal noise standard deviations (in normalized input units) the degradation curve samples; include 0.0 for the clean reference
fields.draws_per_count: Number of random channel subsets averaged for each dropped-channel count
fields.seed: Seed of the noise draws and dropped-channel subsets
fields.figure_style: PlotBase figure style the severity curves are rendered with (report or paper)
fields.noise_draws: Number of independent noise draws averaged per sigma and channel; more draws tighten the error bars at linear cost
fields.gain_factors: Global input gain factors of the calibration-error sweep; 1.0 is always included as the reference
fields.shift_pixels: Row shifts in pixels of the shift-equivariance stress; each must stay below the patch height

diagnostics::TrainingEvolutionConfig.summary: Entry config that animates how one or more backbone runs learned: the split re-predicted from every saved epoch snapshot, one GIF per target channel with the RMSE of every snapshot, written into each run directory

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for run directories holding the configured checkpoint file; each selected run is animated in sequence
fields.run_filter: Run directory names (or names of parent directories whose nested runs are expanded) to animate; empty selects interactively on a TTY and every discovered run otherwise
fields.split: Dataset split re-predicted at every snapshot
fields.device: Torch device the snapshot evaluations run on
fields.checkpoint_name: Checkpoint filename loaded from each run directory and used as the run-discovery marker; the model is restored to it after the sweep
fields.output_subdir: Name of the output directory created inside each run directory for the GIFs, JSON and markdown report
fields.batch_size: Batch size of the forward passes over the split patches at every snapshot
fields.fps: Frames per second of the rendered GIFs (one frame per epoch snapshot)
fields.figure_style: PlotBase figure style the frames are rendered with (report or paper)

diagnostics::OnnxExportEntryConfig.summary: Entry config that rebuilds each selected backbone run's model, loads its best checkpoint and exports the forward as an ONNX graph with a manifest

fields.runs_dir: root directory scanned recursively for runs holding a best_model.pt with backbone meta files; each becomes one export
fields.run_filter: substrings a run's relative name must contain to be exported; empty exports every discovered run
fields.opset: ONNX opset version the exported graph targets
fields.dynamic_batch: whether the exported input and params output keep a dynamic batch axis instead of the fixed export batch of one

diagnostics::ResultTableEntryConfig.summary: Entry config that exports one table row per run with finished inference: a CSV with every scalar metric plus LaTeX and markdown tables with the selected columns

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for runs holding a finished inference; each run becomes one table row
fields.run_filter: Substrings a run's relative name must contain to be exported; empty exports every discovered run
fields.split: Data split the exported inference stamp of every run must have been scored on (train, val or test), read from the stamp's completion marker
fields.inference_subdir: Fixed inference stamp to read metrics from; it must carry a completion marker for the configured split, and empty picks each run's newest completed stamp of that split, skipping stamps without a completion marker with a warning
fields.metrics_filename: Metrics filename read inside the resolved inference stamp
fields.metrics: Metric keys forming the LaTeX and markdown columns, in order; empty renders every scalar key seen across the runs
fields.sort_by: Metric key the rows are ordered by; empty keeps discovery order
fields.ascending: Whether the sort_by ordering is ascending (best-first for losses) rather than descending
fields.precision: Significant digits used for the LaTeX and markdown cells; the CSV always keeps full precision
fields.output_dir: Directory receiving results_table.csv, results_table.tex and results_table.md

diagnostics::PaperFigurePackConfig.summary: Entry config that packs inference figures from selected runs into the publication figures directory under stable names with a JSON manifest of every source

fields.runs_dir: Root directory scanned recursively for runs holding a finished inference report; each selected run contributes figures
fields.run_filter: Run directory names (or names of parent directories whose nested runs are expanded) to pack; empty selects interactively on a TTY and every discovered run otherwise
fields.split: Data split the packed inference stamp of every run must have been scored on (train, val or test), read from the stamp's completion marker
fields.inference_subdir: Fixed inference stamp to read figures from; it must carry a completion marker for the configured split, and empty picks each run's newest completed stamp of that split, skipping stamps without a completion marker with a warning
fields.metrics_filename: Filename marking a finished inference when resolving the latest stamp
fields.report_filename: Report filename used as the run-discovery marker
fields.figures_subdir: Name of the figures directory inside each inference stamp the patterns are matched against
fields.patterns: Glob patterns relative to the figures directory selecting which figures enter the pack
fields.output_dir: Publication figures directory the stable-named copies and the manifest are written into

diagnostics::TrainingProfileEntryConfig.summary: Entry config that records full training steps of one backbone under torch.profiler and writes a chrome trace, an operator table and a top-operator summary

fields.model_name: backbone registry key building the profiled workload; empty picks resunet
fields.gpu: index of the GPU the profiled steps execute on
fields.seed: random seed for sampling and model initialisation
fields.use_amp: whether the profiled forward runs under bfloat16 autocast, matching a mixed-precision training run
fields.num_workers: data loader worker processes during profiling
fields.warmup_steps: steps the profiler observes without recording, letting allocator and autotune effects settle
fields.active_steps: steps recorded into the trace and the operator statistics
fields.record_shapes: record operator input shapes, enabling shape-grouped views in the trace viewer
fields.profile_memory: record allocator events so the trace shows per-operator memory traffic
fields.with_stack: record Python stacks per operator; the trace grows considerably
fields.paths: dataset and run path configuration the feed adapter reads
fields.output_dir: directory receiving one timestamped profile directory per run

generation::GenerationConfig.summary: Shape of the synthetic dense regression dataset: grid size, input channels, field smoothness, the neighbourhood of the local target, noise levels and the split fractions

fields.output_directory: directory the dataset is written into; it must not exist yet, so a finished dataset is never overwritten
fields.input_channels: number of input fields x0, x1, ...; the targets read x0 to x3, so at least four are needed and any further channel is a pure distractor
fields.smoothing_pixels: standard deviation in pixels of the normal smoothing kernel that turns white noise into each smooth input field
fields.neighbourhood: side in pixels of the square window the neighbourhood target averages over, which sets the receptive field a model needs to predict it
fields.input_noise: standard deviation of the white noise added to every standardized input field
fields.target_noise: standard deviation of the white noise added to every target field
fields.val_fraction: share of the rows held out as the validation band, below the training band
fields.test_fraction: share of the rows held out as the test band, at the bottom of the grid
fields.seed: seed of the random generator drawing every field and noise sample

generation::GenerateDatasetEntryConfig.summary: Entry config of generate_dataset: the generation settings and the log directory

fields.generation: GenerationConfig describing the grid, the fields and the splits
fields.log_dir: directory the generation log is written into
